semantic_adjudication.reason: PlantUML lines 4, 11, and 18 declare or reference a state named Idle inside three different sub-machine blocks. PlantUML resolves same-named states as global identifiers, so these three declarations collapse into one state (CollisionAvoidanceSystem.Frontend.Idle). The closed model contains only a single Idle state. The author's intent for three independent collision avoidance modes (per NL2 and NL3) requires three separate Idle states, one per mode. The alternative that the model is 'consistent with itself' acknowledges the divergence between author intent and the produced model rather than providing a competing reading of the obligation.

decisions.basis: NL2 requirement text; PlantUML line 25 unconditional arrow; FCSTM transition:line:45 with empty trigger set; S3 predicate receipt (verdict=false, counterexample expected=['Collision Detected'], observed=[])
decisions.reason: NL2 explicitly states the sub-machine 'becomes active when' collision is detected, making the trigger a property of the activation/entry. The S3 predicate confirms the exact mismatch: expected triggers ['Collision Detected'] vs observed []. The alternative reading that collision events trigger internal transitions is defeated because 'becomes active when' refers to the state's own activation, not to post-entry internal behavior. The unconditional initial entry means the state is always active upon system start, contradicting the event-conditional activation the NL requires.
decisions.violated_obligation: The entry transition into CollisionAvoidanceSystem should carry a collision detection trigger as required by NL2 ('becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected'), but the only root-level entry transition (line:45) has an empty trigger set.

decisions.basis: NL3 requirement text; canonical source IR concurrent_regions count=0; PlantUML source lines 2-24 showing no -- separators; FCSTM state inventory showing all three children in one implicit region
decisions.reason: NL3 uses the specific UML term 'orthogonal regions' and explicitly requires 'concurrent activation of different collision avoidance controls.' The canonical source IR reports concurrent_regions count=0, and the PlantUML source contains no -- separator lines within the CollisionAvoidanceSystem block. The alternative that children could be entered independently via separate parent edges does not address the orthogonal region requirement, which is a distinct structural property in UML semantics. No competing reading of 'orthogonal regions' is supported by the supplied facts.
decisions.violated_obligation: NL3 requires orthogonal regions in CollisionAvoidanceSystem to enable concurrent activation of different collision avoidance controls, but the model contains zero concurrent regions (no UML -- separators); all three child composites reside in a single implicit region.

decisions.basis: NL2 requirement text; complete FCSTM transition inventory (26 transitions); S2 predicate receipt (verdict=false); transition:line:44 (only outgoing from CollisionAvoidanceSystem is exit); transition:line:45 (root entry lacks collision trigger)
decisions.reason: The complete FCSTM transition inventory (26 transitions) was examined and contains no transition from CollisionAvoidanceSystem to any of Frontend, RearEnd, or Pedestrian with a collision detection trigger. The only outgoing transition from CollisionAvoidanceSystem is the exit to [*]. The S2 predicate confirms no transition exists between the bound source and target. The alternative that sub-machines could be entered via their own initial pseudostates is defeated because CollisionAvoidanceSystem's initial edge targets the synthetic UnspecifiedInitial, not any child composite. The alternative that 'enclosing state' means root is also defeated because the root-to-CollisionAvoidanceSystem transition (line:45) also lacks a collision detection trigger.

decisions.basis: NL2 requirement text; verify_facts non_proved reachability for Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian; inspection_equivalent_facts reachable_state_count=3, unreachable_state_count=8; reachable_state_refs=[root, CollisionAvoidanceSystem, UnspecifiedInitial]

issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.

issues.basis: NL3 text; PlantUML source lines 2-24 showing CollisionAvoidanceSystem with three child composites and no -- separators; canonical source IR concurrent_regions count=0; FCSTM state:CollisionAvoidanceSystem:line:6 with children Frontend:line:7, RearEnd:line:25, Pedestrian:line:30 all in same implicit region; inspection facts showing all three unreachable (confirming no concurrent activation path exists).
issues.expected: CollisionAvoidanceSystem should contain orthogonal region separators (UML -- divisions) that partition the three collision avoidance modes (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian) into concurrent regions enabling simultaneous activation.
issues.observed: CollisionAvoidanceSystem contains three child composites (Frontend line 7, RearEnd line 25, Pedestrian line 30) in a single implicit region with no separators. The canonical source IR reports concurrent_regions count=0. The PlantUML source shows no -- lines within the CollisionAvoidanceSystem block. All three children are sequential alternatives in one region, not concurrent orthogonal partitions.
issues.reason: NL3 explicitly requires 'orthogonal regions' for 'concurrent activation of different collision avoidance controls.' The closed model shows CollisionAvoidanceSystem with child states but zero concurrent regions (no separators). This is a region_structure violation: the required orthogonal partitioning is absent. No frozen predicate directly expresses region structure, so predicate_id is null.

issues.strongest_rebuttal: The three child composites each have their own internal initial entry and could be entered independently if the parent had separate entry edges to each. However, UML orthogonal regions require explicit separators for true concurrency; without them, the composites are structurally sequential alternatives within one region, and the parent's single default entry to UnspecifiedInitial confirms they cannot be concurrently activated.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidanceSystem lacks orthogonal region separators for concurrent activation

issues.basis: NL2; FCSTM complete transition inventory: 26 transitions, none from CollisionAvoidanceSystem to Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian; semantic_bindings BIND-NL2-SOURCE-ENCLOSING (exact) and BIND-NL2-TARGET-SUBMACHINE (ambiguous); source_inventory transitions tr_0001-tr_0014 show no parent-to-child entry transitions with collision events.
issues.expected: A transition from CollisionAvoidanceSystem (the enclosing state) to at least one collision avoidance sub-machine (Frontend, RearEnd, or Pedestrian) triggered by a collision detection event (Collision_Detected or equivalent).
issues.observed: The complete FCSTM transition inventory (26 transitions) contains no transition from state:CollisionAvoidanceSystem:line:6 to state:Frontend:line:7, state:RearEnd:line:25, or state:Pedestrian:line:30 with any collision detection trigger. The only outgoing transition from CollisionAvoidanceSystem is transition:line:44 to [*] (exit) guarded by R45RouteToken==14.
issues.reason: The NL2 contract requires an entry transition from the enclosing state to the collision avoidance sub-machine upon collision detection. The exact source (CollisionAvoidanceSystem) is bound, but the target is ambiguous between three child composites. Regardless of which target is intended, NO transition from the source to ANY of the three targets with a collision detection trigger exists in the complete inventory. The predicate is null because S2 requires one exact source-target pair and the target identity is ambiguous.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The sub-machines could be entered via their own initial pseudostates when CollisionAvoidanceSystem is activated, but no such initial entry path exists: CollisionAvoidanceSystem's initial edge targets the synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state, not any child composite. Alternatively, the 'enclosing state' might refer to the root rather than CollisionAvoidanceSystem, but the root-to-CollisionAvoidanceSystem transition (line:45) also has no collision detection trigger.
issues.title: No collision-detection-triggered entry transition from enclosing state to any collision avoidance sub-machine

issues.observed: All three sub-machines are unreachable: verify_facts refutes reachability for Frontend (state:Frontend:line:7), RearEnd (state:RearEnd:line:25), and Pedestrian (state:Pedestrian:line:30). No transition path exists from CollisionAvoidanceSystem to any child composite.
issues.reason: NL2 requires the sub-machine to become active upon collision detection, which presupposes reachability. The derived reachability contract captures the behavioral consequence that none of the three collision avoidance sub-machines can ever be entered in the closed model, making the required activation behavior impossible. G1 is used with source=CollisionAvoidanceSystem (reachable) and target=Frontend (unreachable) as the representative pair; RearEnd and Pedestrian share the identical defect.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The sub-machines are structurally present and contain valid internal behavior (Idle->Braking->Clamping->Idle cycle). If an external mechanism were to enter them, their internal behavior would function correctly. However, no such entry mechanism exists in the closed model.
issues.title: All three collision avoidance sub-machines are unreachable from root initial entry

issues.basis: NL2; FCSTM transition:line:39 (source=[*], target=UnspecifiedInitial, scope=CollisionAvoidanceSystem); working_contract compiler_owned element compiler:state:llms_emp_feedback_final_0047.CollisionAvoidanceSystem.UnspecifiedInitial (kind=synthetic_state); verify_facts proved initial-entry:transition:line:39 (edge exists but targets synthetic); source_inventory: no transition from @initial:CollisionAvoidanceSystem to any child state; PlantUML source: CollisionAvoidanceSystem block contains no [*] --> child directive.
issues.expected: CollisionAvoidanceSystem should have an initial entry edge targeting at least one of its author-specified child composites (Frontend, RearEnd, or Pedestrian) so that collision avoidance behavior can begin upon system activation.
issues.observed: CollisionAvoidanceSystem's only initial pseudostate edge is transition:line:39 ([*] -> UnspecifiedInitial), which targets a compiler-synthetic state (working_contract kind=synthetic_state) created to handle the absent author-specified initial target. No initial edge from CollisionAvoidanceSystem's [*] to Frontend, RearEnd, or Pedestrian exists.
issues.reason: The derived initial_entry contract captures the structural root cause of the sub-machines' unreachability. CollisionAvoidanceSystem semantically owns the collision avoidance behavior (it is the parent of all three sub-machines) but lacks a proper default entry to any of them. The compiler created a synthetic placeholder (UnspecifiedInitial) because the author did not specify an initial target. This is a distinct property from reachability: it identifies the exact owner-local defect (missing initial edge to a valid child) rather than the global consequence (children unreachable from root). Predicate is null because the exact target of the required initial entry is ambiguous (could be Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian, or all three for concurrent semantics).
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.

However, this only allows termination, not activation of any collision avoidance sub-machine. The author's PlantUML source shows no [*] --> within CollisionAvoidanceSystem targeting a specific child, confirming the initial target was genuinely unspecified by the author.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidanceSystem initial entry targets compiler-synthetic placeholder instead of any collision avoidance sub-machine
